title: NoiseFile
shortDescription: Know local noise rules, measure incidents, and prepare the right complaint.
fullDescription:
NoiseFile helps Bay Area residents understand local noise rules, document disturbances, and take the correct official next step.

KNOW WHAT COUNTS
Choose your city and the source: animal, general neighborhood noise, or construction. NoiseFile explains the applicable hours, published thresholds or plainly-audible standard, required incident history, evidence still needed, and the agency responsible for the complaint.

MEASURE AND DOCUMENT
Run a live estimated sound meter and save the incident's time, duration, minimum, average, and maximum reading. Add the location, impact, and notes while the facts are fresh. The city-rule check explains why the incident does or does not meet the condition the phone can evaluate—and plainly says when the city's rule depends on evidence beyond a decibel reading.

PREPARE THE NEXT STEP
NoiseFile builds organized complaint text from the saved incident and the local rule. Copy it before opening the official city form, share an incident-history report, or use the verified phone or email route when no online form is available.

LOCAL COVERAGE
The offline catalog includes 45 animal, general-noise, and construction workflows across San Jose, San Francisco, Oakland, Fremont, Santa Rosa, Hayward, Concord, Sunnyvale, Santa Clara, Vallejo, Berkeley, Richmond, Antioch, Daly City, and San Mateo.

PRIVATE BY DESIGN
No account. No ads. No analytics. Incident history stays in private storage on the device unless you explicitly share it. Raw microphone audio is processed for the meter and is not saved or uploaded.

IMPORTANT
Phone sound readings are estimates, not calibrated enforcement measurements. Local officials make the final determination under their required equipment, position, duration, and other conditions. NoiseFile provides procedural information and is not legal advice.
